title: I got sick of AI 3D models having the clothes fused to the body, so I made a free browser tool that cuts them apart by painting
author: Middle-Moist
selftext:
Every character I got out of an AI generator had the shirt, belt, knife and boots all melted into one mesh with the body. Fitting things was atrocious and splitting them in Blender meant selecting thousands of faces by hand, every single time, and I'm not equipped for that. So I built MeshShears.

You drop your model in, paint each part a different colour, hit export, and you get a zip with every piece as its own GLB, still the right size and the right way up, with its texture. The fill follows colour edges and folds, so a whole shirt is usually a click or two. If you don't feel like painting, there's a Find pieces button that runs Segment Anything right in your browser and guesses the parts for you. Then you drag a slider to make the pieces bigger or smaller and split or join whatever it got wrong.

There's also a clone brush for painting over spots, like where a strap was baked into the cloth texture. Also let's me do final passes after things get fitted to do final touch ups. It opens GLB, glTF, OBJ, FBX, STL and PLY. It uses your graphics card if you have one, and nothing ever gets uploaded, so it runs entirely on your machine and works offline.

It's free and open source (MIT). I made it for pulling clothes and gear off characters so I can refit and swap them, but it works for cleaning up scans or prepping any model for Unity, Unreal, Godot or Blender.

Try it here: https://khelevaster-ship-it.github.io/Meshshears/

Code: https://github.com/khelevaster-ship-it/Meshshears

Would love to hear what breaks it. Throw your worst models at it and let me know.

comments.author: VictorBuildsApps
comments.body: When I made the gear rigid inside a one-mesh character, pinning its weights to one bone, it still bent 9-22 mm in poses, because its edge had to stretch and there was no coat under it. In the end I regenerated the character without the gear and generated the map case on its own. Does MeshShears do anything about the hole a piece leaves behind once it's cut out, or is that a Blender job afterward?

replies.author: Middle-Moist
replies.body:
Yeah that matches what I found, rigid stuff baked into a skinned mesh always bends somewhere. Generating the gear separately is honestly the cleanest way if you can.

MeshShears doesn't patch the hole with new geometry, the cloth under the gear was never generated so there's nothing to recover. What I do instead is two passes on the same model. First pass I paint the gear as its own piece and export it. Second pass I paint those same faces back as part of the coat and use the clone brush to paint real cloth texture over where the gear was, then export the coat whole. You end up with a coat that has no hole and no gear printed on it, plus the gear as a separate rigid prop you can parent to one bone. If the gear stuck out a lot, the coat can have a bump there, and smoothing that is still a quick Blender job.

replies.author: Middle-Moist
replies.body: I am adding that feature now. It will now self patch the holes left behind with the surrounding mesh

comments.author: Not-a-Clever-UN
comments.body:
I built a similar tool for my own use.  Gives me a unique position to tell you what I fixed with mine... and lets me see what you did better than me, lol.

* Meshshears wall tool goes all the way through a model, eg cut an arm and it'll go through the torso and the other arm.  In mine I had it add actual plane objects you can adjust the edges of and it automatically stops after going through two walls.   You could also ask your agent to add "cuts that walk a closed ring."  


* your interface is much better. I started mine with sol 5.6 and I think even after asking newer models to fix it, still has baggage from that initial bad design. 
* claude says your fill works better 

My tool also does more (like I can step the model through animation frames and toggle on displaying rigging), which is in some ways, worse.  There's kind of a continuum between "simple like phone editing a picture" and "as complicated as blender."  Mine has moved more complicated.  So, in short, I might recommend deciding what your tool *doesn't* do.  I've had to start resisting adding things, because I could easily see it bloating to "blender like" proportions as I add every little thing I think could be somewhat useful.  

I've never shared my tool, because well, it's kind of ugly and the gui sucks and I don't want to listen to people tell me that. I know, lol.

replies.author: Middle-Moist
replies.body:
Id be interested in heading how to make mine more dependable especially in regards to the find the pieces part. I just finished the second part of the pipeline and will opensource it next. Exact same ui but it let's you take the pieces and the body you want, fill in holes, put them on and fit it yourself. it works really well and i can now cut, fit, and export to claude for motion checks in under an hour per model. This is my two tools and 45 minutes of my time, vs claude on fable 5.2 high on retry 18. The end goal is a system that can auto fit 100ks of thousands of villagers across 6 ages with different attire based on profession, culture, and climate. 1500 costumes planned for overall

https://i.redd.it/m4jgjtt49g3i1.jpeg

replies.author: Not-a-Clever-UN
replies.body:
I haven't found anything super reliable in terms of algorithms, especially since there's texture over-spray that makes "by color" unreliable.  I might suggest instead doing one piece of clothing at a time as a stand alone object, or on a generic "mannequin" or if that doesn't quite work, maybe prompt a person in a bright contrast color morph suit (like pink).    Then have the agent scale the person to an exact size in each dimension (based on the exposed parts of the body) before doing the cutting away, so the outputs are matched size. 

Exposure is the only algorithm that was somewhat useful, but it still failed to get me clean output and I have to do cleanup each time.  I might try doing something that uses information from all the approaches and like, averages them, but I need to find more approaches for that to work out.  So far, counting your approach, I have maybe 4 decent ones, and like 7 that didn't produce anything useful.
